2608.21487.title: TASSO: TAsk-Specific Subspace Optimization for Continual Learning of Vision-Language Models
2608.21487.paper_summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot capabilities, making them an attractive solution for continual learning across diverse tasks. However, during continual adaptation, both catastrophic forgetting and zero-shot degradation occur, severely degrading performance. In this paper, we introduce TASSO, a new paradigm that efficiently preserves the latent space geometry while ensuring network plasticity. We achieve this with two complementary techniques: subspace learning and geometry-aware knowledge distillation. Specifically, we first learn a sequence of task-specific low-rank projectors, which we use to project the latent representations before optimizing cross-entropy. Secondly, we employ a geodesic-distance-based loss that distills knowledge from the previous-task model while effectively preserving the latent space geometry. These design choices not only avoid unnecessary parameter updates along the full embedding dimensions but also improve learning by focusing on task-specific manifolds. Moreover, the geometry-aware distillation provides strong regularization and significantly reduces both catastrophic forgetting and zero-shot degradation throughout the continual learning sequence. Experimental results with the CLIP vision language model in the multi-domain task incremental and class incremental learning benchmarks demonstrate clear improvements over state-of-the-art methods in mitigating forgetting and preserving zero-shot capabilities.
2608.21487.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型（VLMs）展現出強大的零-shot 能力，使其成為在多樣任務中進行持續學習的理想解決方案。<lb/>然而，在持續適應過程中，會發生災難性遺忘和零-shot 降級，嚴重影響性能。<lb/>在本文中，我們介紹了 TASSO，一種新範式，能有效地保留潛在空間幾何，同時確保網絡的可塑性。<lb/>我們通過兩種互補技術實現這一目標：子空間學習和幾何感知知識蒸餾。<lb/>具體來說，我們首先學習一系列任務特定的低秩投影器，並在優化交叉熵之前使用它們來投影潛在表示。<lb/>其次，我們採用基於測地距離的損失，從前一任務模型中提取知識，同時有效保留潛在空間幾何。<lb/>這些設計選擇不僅避免了沿著完整嵌入維度的不必要參數更新，還通過專注於任務特定流形來改善學習。<lb/>此外，幾何感知蒸餾提供了強大的正則化，並顯著減少了在整個持續學習序列中的災難性遺忘和零-shot 降級。<lb/>在多領域任務增量和類別增量學習基準中，使用 CLIP 視覺語言模型的實驗結果顯示，在減輕遺忘和保留零-shot 能力方面，相較於最先進的方法有明顯改善。
